title: The repo-root secrets manifest is the single source of truth for what secrets exist
description: A file named `secrets.yaml` at the repo root enumerates every secret the project depends on. Each entry declares a stable logical name, the path or reference the vendor uses to fetch the value, the owner, the rotation-days budget, the environment scope (declared as an environment-aware structure whose exact shape is elicited from the operator; the common default is `dev`, `ci`, `live`), and whether the secret is required or optional. Nothing outside the manifest may declare a secret dependency; a required secret referenced from code but absent from the manifest is a build refusal. Secret VALUES never appear in the manifest; only names, paths, and metadata.
rationale: A scattered secret dependency graph is the failure mode this blueprint exists to end. If every code path names its own environment variable, no one knows what the project actually needs, rotation is guesswork, and a missing secret surfaces as a runtime null. A single manifest at a known path makes the dependency set legible to humans, to CI gates, to onboarding runs, and to the vendor-side least-privilege policy that grants access to exactly the declared set.
